results.title: [PDF] SGD Noise and Implicit Low-Rank Bias in Deep Neural Networks
results.content: CBMM Memo No. 134 March 28, 2022 SGD Noise and Implicit Low-Rank Bias in Deep Neural Networks Tomer Galanti and Tomaso Poggio Center for Brains, Minds, and Machines, MIT, Cambridge, MA, USA Abstract We analyze deep ReLU neural networks trained with mini-batch stochastic gradient decent and weight decay. Furthermore, we show, both theoretically and empirically, that when training a neural network using Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with a small batch size, the resulting weight matrices are expected to be of small rank. Furthermore, we show, both theoretically and empirically, that when training a neural network using SGD with a small batch size, the resulting weight matrices are expected to be of small rank. We made the several key theoretical and empirical observations: • We show that the batch size, weight decay and learning rate contribute to a regularizing effect on the rank of the trainable matrices of neural networks; • Weight decay and training with mini-batches are necessary to obtain rank minimization; • SGD noise is inevitable when applying weight decay.
